docs.title: Axon Vehicle Intelligence — Outpost, Lightpost, and the Streetlight as a Sensor
docs.blurb: Axon moved its cameras off officers and onto street furniture. What Outpost and Lightpost actually are, what they can recognise, what cities paid, and the accuracy numbers nobody has published.

headline.title: HEADLINE FINDING — THE MOUNT IS THE PRODUCT, NOT THE CAMERA
headline.body: The Axis plate camera and the Ubicquia streetlight node are both commodity parts. What is new is that bolting them together collapses a fixed camera from a civil-works project into a one-hour service call — and collapses the political cost from a siting hearing into an attachment agreement. Cameras cheap to install are installed in quantity, and can be re-aimed at a different street in an hour with no procurement event. Meanwhile Axon publishes no accuracy figure, no false-positive rate, and no product-level retention standard.
